issues.description: Extraction requires data/stories/manifest.json and story files that are absent from the repo, so the advertised tiny demo and integration test fail.
Default stories_dir points to data/stories, but that directory contains no corpus files.
Documentation claims stories can be loaded or generated and that tiny demo runs, but no generation path exists and fresh execution fails.
pca_components_for_variance accepts threshold 0 but still returns one component, making it impossible to disable PCA projection via config.
Validation loads vector metadata but does not verify backend/model/dimension compatibility before instantiating a possibly different backend.
Preference validation has the same missing vector/backend compatibility check and can crash or produce invalid comparisons.
HF dtype='auto' is ignored and the model is loaded without device_map, increasing the chance of avoidable CPU/GPU memory failures.
Preference scoring uses only the first token of encoded ' good' and ' bad', which is tokenizer-dependent and can silently score the wrong token.
Tiny backend emotion detection uses substring counts, causing false positives such as matching emotion cues inside unrelated words.
Validation scenarios reuse lexical cues from the tiny backend lexicon, so tiny-mode success is partly baked into the test data.
RunConfig coerces values but does not validate required fields, ranges, or non-empty emotion/topic counts before pipeline execution.
Empty story/config inputs can reach min/max over an empty start_positions list instead of failing early with a clear configuration error.
Configured steering.min_reported_emotions is ignored; the implementation hard-codes four steered emotions.
The only integration test depends on missing external story files and currently fails from a clean checkout.
Tests use config.yaml relative to the process working directory, making them brittle outside the repo root.
Test extras include pytest only and no lint/type tooling, leaving most backend and configuration problems unchecked.
Generated demo outputs, including binary artifacts, are committed while the source data needed to reproduce them is missing.
